info.title: Vectory control plane
info.description:
The HTTP API behind the Vectory dashboard. Everything the dashboard does goes through it.

**Authentication.** Sign in with `POST /api/v1/login`. The reply sets the `vectory_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, 12 hours) and returns a `csrf_token`. Send the cookie with every request, and the token as the `X-CSRF-Token` header with every `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE`. Requests run with your role. There are no separate API keys.

**Agent protocol.** `/agent/v1/` operations are served only on the separate agent listener and authenticate devices with mutual TLS. A device ID in a request body is never trusted for authentication.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Common: UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, STALE_REVISION, INVALID_INPUT, RATE_LIMITED, SIGNIN_THROTTLED, CAPACITY_BUSY (agent listener or download slots busy, or a membership preview found the writer busy; retry after Retry-After), REQUEST_TIMEOUT (agent request deadline), PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (body over its limit), EXPORT_BUSY, EXPORT_CAPACITY, EXPORT_STORAGE, EXPORT_TIMEOUT, EXPORT_TOO_LARGE, VALIDATION_FAILED, INTERNAL. AccessEditRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped exact-target access edit status. An applied user is the immutable public commit snapshot, not necessarily the account’s current state. not_found is noncausal while a PUT may be in flight; cancellation fences only an absent request and cannot undo an applied edit.

Person.description: Administrator view of one account. invited means no password has been chosen yet; invite_expires_at is the live invitation expiry, if any.

UserRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped, secret-free current status. not_found is not cancellation: an in-flight POST may still commit. A repeated keyed POST always conflicts; cancel fences a late create only when it wins the writer transaction.

ResetRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped, exact-target, secret-free reset issuance status. A negative read does not fence an in-flight POST. Issued active is true only while this exact code verifier remains current and unexpired for an enabled account. Cancellation revokes the exact still-current unused code and fences late issuance; it cannot undo a code already redeemed.

configuration_mode.description: Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.

retry_preconditions.description: Retry requires the reviewed desired version and generation plus current retryable state and enabled sync.

desired_sha256.description: Exact rendered artifact digest for the currently released device generation. Version identity, delivered artifact bytes, and actual managed-file digest are distinct.

reported_apply_state.description: Agent-reported workload state, separate from progress of the current desired assignment.

vector_log_summary.description: Latest summary from an agent that reports it; absent for agents that do not.

evaluations.description: Evaluations on this version, counted up to the canary measurement count (3 by default; editable under Settings → Notifications → Detection, 1 to 20).

issue_count.description: Open issues on this version. List rows (DeviceListItem) carry only the first of them in issues.

data_plane.description: Data-plane health measured from telemetry on the version the device verifiably runs; absent until the first evaluation. The device reads Degraded while status is verified, version_id equals desired_version_id and issues is nonempty.

check_in_seconds.description: Current check-in interval; until the agent acknowledges a policy change, the longer of the old and new interval.

running_version.description: Last verified managed version on the host, which keeps running after a failed update or a removed assignment. Null means no managed version was ever verified (the host runs its adopted local config).

check_in_seconds.description: Longest interval the agent may currently take between check-ins.

timeline.description: Recorded apply-state changes after release, oldest first. Heartbeats can skip states.

request_id.description: Optional durable create identity scoped to the authenticated actor. Reuse only with the identical payload.

replaces.description: Existing assignments of the same resource that this deployment explicitly replaces on the selected devices. Until this deployment releases a device the replaced assignment keeps it; each release retires the replaced assignment there (history kept, persistent selectors exclude the device). An assignment left with nothing to deliver is retired (status unassigned, status_before_removal kept). Without replaces, equal-priority different payloads still conflict. A replaced assignment that changed or no longer selects any of these devices returns 409 REPLACEMENT_CHANGED.

policy_id.description: Saved agent settings a policy deployment applies. The policy must equal their current values, otherwise preview and creation return 409.

DeploymentReceipt.description: Current original result with response-only durable request identity. For rollback, result ID differs from source ID. Mutable deployment state and targets need not equal the original request.

DeploymentRequestStatus.description: Outer request_id, operation and source_deployment_id must exactly match the nested receipt and the locally frozen operation. A negative read is not proof an in-flight request failed.

outcome.description: replace: the device moves from the listed replaced assignment when this deployment releases it.

winner.description: The assignment that currently wins for this device and resource, possibly not yet released.

replaces.description: The requested replacement that covers this device.

request_correlation.description: Keyed create/rollback receipts and exact request lookup echo durable request, operation and source identity.

replacements.description: The effect of the requested replaces list. retires_assignment is true when nothing is left for the replaced assignment to deliver, including future members of a persistent selector.

suggested_replaces.description: Current winners of the same pipeline (or any agent settings) with a different payload, which a reviewed deployment would normally replace.

suggested_priority.description: Highest priority among suggested replacements, to reuse.

configuration_name.description: Current name of the pipeline whose version is previewed; null for agent settings. Omitted by older servers.

winning_priority.description: Lowest priority that would outrank every existing winner on conflicting or outranked devices, when one exists.

paused_device_ids.description: Configuration targets whose sync is paused; they apply the change after sync resumes.

created_by.description: Token list only: the account that created it (recovery: authorized it).

last_used_at.description: Token list only: when it last enrolled a device.

device_count.description: Token list only: devices it enrolled.

devices.description: Token list only: most recently enrolled devices.

TokenRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped exact creation identity. Lookup never reveals a secret. A negative read is not cancellation; cancellation fences late creation and revokes the mapped token atomically.

DeviceRecoveryRequestStatus.description: Current administrator own recovery request bound to its original device UUID. Record recovery_device_id must equal envelope device_id, and recovery_name must equal the reviewed expected_name. No secret replay. A negative read does not fence late issuance. Cancellation revokes only the mapped token; completed replacement identities remain unchanged.

DeviceRecoveryRequest.description: Empty legacy request or strict correlated request. The expected name must exactly match the original source device on first issuance. Same actor/request key cannot be rebound to another device or reviewed name.

catalog_problems.description: Why catalog entries are not offered; administrators only, empty for other roles.

source.description: bundled with the server image, or from the operator mirror, which replaces a platform bundled build

static_checked.description: The isolated worker ran pinned Vector on this draft (with placeholders and stand-ins where only a device can resolve a value).

deferred.description: Each device still checks environment, secrets, files or platform before applying.

placeholders.description: Secret and environment references that were replaced by typed placeholders for the static check.

not_run.description: True when Vector did not run this test, for example because another test could not be read or built. Such a test never passes.

outputs.description: Output payloads Vector printed for a failed test, from the draft's synthetic test inputs.

port.description: Named output, or an empty string for the default output.

timestamps.description: Flattened field paths whose values are timestamps.

configuration_mode.description: Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.
Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.

diagnostics.description: Structured findings the agent or the server reports about a device, errors first, at most 10.

vector_log_summary.description: Sent only to servers that list the feature; an empty list means nothing to report.

sha256.description: Digest of exact target-specific rendered artifact bytes, not necessarily the published base-version digest.

features.description: Additive heartbeat fields this server accepts (diagnostics, host_runtime, vector_log_summary, telemetry_v2). Agents send those fields only when listed, so older servers keep their strict validation. Unknown names are ignored.

payload.description: Exact UTF-8 JSON Manifest bytes, decoded before signature verification

signature.description: Ed25519 signature over exact decoded payload

HostRuntime.description: What the host contributes beyond the signed artifact. data_dir_source: pipeline (the configuration sets data_dir), host (install --vector-data-dir), adopted (the adopted configuration's data_dir), vector_default (Vector's own default exists and is writable), agent_default (a private directory the agent created). The host value reaches Vector through a separate runtime file, so the managed artifact digest is unchanged. metrics_source: explicit (local metrics URL), discovered (a loopback prometheus_exporter sink in the running configuration) or none. activation: how the last change was activated (reload via SIGHUP with verified completion, or restart).

VectorLogGroup.description: Recent Vector WARN/ERROR log lines grouped by a fingerprint of component and normalized message. Messages are redacted like diagnostics. Counts are since the agent started.

CanaryGate.description: Read-only current canary evidence, separate from historical progress. Each released target contributes exactly once to verified_count or one reason. Only observing has a nonnull observation start and requires every released target to be currently verified. Counts and evaluation share a read snapshot; no countdown or future release promise.

artifact_sha256.description: Null when the device had no previously managed version before this deployment; the preview is then blocked with PRIOR_VERSION_UNKNOWN.

RollbackPreview.description: Complete metadata-only historical scope, bounded to 10000 distinct device UUIDs across both lists. Ready requires at least one eligible device, a common previous version and no blockers. Each eligible target exposes the exact prior artifact digest, never its bytes or binding values. Names are display-only. The token binds source, exact eligible/excluded identities and reasons, prior version, prior target artifact digests and generations, admission and current assignment state.

AssignmentRemovalPreview.description: Read-only removal simulation. Every device identity is distinct, ready is true exactly when blockers is empty, and an empty ready scope is allowed. Fingerprint binds the actor, source and meaningful current/projected delivery state, not display metadata or telemetry. Configuration removal can retain local workload; policy removal can restore defaults. Pending candidates are not delivered assignments.

ScheduledRefreshPreview.description: Read-only comparison of the saved scheduled snapshot and current selector resolution. Device identities are distinct within each list; the combined union is bounded to10000. Ready is true exactly when blockers is empty; an empty proposed selection is blocked. New UUIDs without complete typed bindings produce VARIABLE_BINDING_REQUIRED; the actor-bound token covers frozen bindings, source settings, saved/proposed membership and an internal monotonic revision so delayed requests cannot overwrite a newer review, including an ABA change. Matching no-op does not mutate or audit. Names and connection status are display metadata. Current saved selection does not attribute an earlier request or establish activation.

coverage.description: Number of fresh device samples that reported each total. Compare with devices_reporting to state partial coverage.

TelemetrySummary.description: Fleet totals from each non-revoked device's latest sample when it is fresh (at most max(180 s, three check-ins) old), plus a downsampled series (per-device mean within each step, summed across devices). A total no fresh device reported is null, never zero.

device_ids.description: Devices whose fresh samples are included.

coverage.description: Number of fresh device samples that reported each total. Compare with devices_reporting to state partial coverage.

anyOf.description: Events per second sent on each named output (route/remap outputs); `_default` is the unnamed output.

VersionTelemetry.description: Per-component rates summed across devices verified to be running this exact version (last verified candidate whose digest still matches the managed file) with fresh samples. Rates sum; *_max fields keep the worst device.

device_ids.description: Devices whose fresh samples are included.

coverage.description: Number of fresh device samples that reported each total. Compare with devices_reporting to state partial coverage.

anyOf.description: Events per second sent on each named output (route/remap outputs); `_default` is the unnamed output.

ConfigurationTelemetry.description: The VersionTelemetry aggregate across every version of one pipeline, with a per-version coverage breakdown (newest version first).

AssignmentDescription.description: Display metadata for an assignment. Names and numbers only: never selectors, targets, variable values or artifacts.

state.description: A failed target state, or degraded: applied but an open DATA_PLANE_* issue on this version (message is its title, diagnostic its reason).

fix.description: Degraded groups only: the issue's fix.

device_ids.description: Every device in the group, bounded; devices lists the first few with names.

RolloutLanes.description: Waves recovered from persisted release times; queued waves follow the scheduler order (pending targets by device ID, canary first, then batches). Failures group current failed targets by diagnostic or error.

DeviceListTelemetry.description: The latest device-level sample. Per-component numbers are on GET /api/v1/devices/{id}.

configuration_mode.description: Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.

status.description: Computed status. awaiting_first_check_in: enrolled but never checked in. offline: more than three check-in intervals late.

retry_preconditions.description: Retry requires the reviewed desired version and generation plus current retryable state and enabled sync.

desired_sha256.description: Exact rendered artifact digest for the currently released device generation. Version identity, delivered artifact bytes, and actual managed-file digest are distinct.

reported_apply_state.description: Agent-reported workload state, separate from progress of the current desired assignment.

evaluations.description: Evaluations on this version, counted up to the canary measurement count (3 by default; editable under Settings → Notifications → Detection, 1 to 20).

issues.description: The first open issue (stalls first), or none; issue_count counts them all.

issue_count.description: Open issues on this version. List rows (DeviceListItem) carry only the first of them in issues.

data_plane.description: Data-plane health measured from telemetry on the version the device verifiably runs; absent until the first evaluation. The device reads Degraded while status is verified, version_id equals desired_version_id and issues is nonempty.

check_in_seconds.description: Current check-in interval; until the agent acknowledges a policy change, the longer of the old and new interval.

running_version.description: Last verified managed version on the host, which keeps running after a failed update or a removed assignment. Null means no managed version was ever verified (the host runs its adopted local config).

DeviceListItem.description: A device as GET /api/v1/devices and the Overview list it: the Device without host_runtime, vector_log_summary and telemetry.components, and with only the first open data-plane issue. GET /api/v1/devices/{id} returns the full Device.

outdated_device_count.description: Applied from this template before its latest edit; they keep the earlier values until it is applied again.

SavedPolicyListItem.description: Applied devices are live devices whose winning settings assignment was applied from this template, or (for assignments made before templates were linked) carries exactly these settings.

GroupMembershipPreview.description: Read-only simulation of a membership edit with the real resolver, rolled back afterwards. pending names a winning assignment that has not released the device yet.

offline_minutes.description: device.offline goes out once an outage lasts this long, measured from the last check-in; a device is offline after three missed check-ins.

pipeline_ids.description: Only events about these pipelines. Empty means every pipeline.

group_ids.description: Only events about devices in these groups (for rollouts: its selector groups and its targets' groups). Empty means every group.

errors_bypass.description: Error-severity problems go out during quiet hours; recoveries and warnings wait.

NotificationRules.description: What a channel sends. Messages held by quiet hours go out as one digest when they end.

allow_private.description: Allows private, CGNAT, unique local and loopback addresses (and plain http:// to them). Link-local, multicast, reserved and cloud metadata addresses are never contacted.

url_hint.description: The saved URL's origin; its path and query are write-only.

security.description: starttls upgrades a plain connection and refuses a server that can't; tls encrypts from the first byte (port 465); none only reaches a relay on the server's own loopback address, with allow_private.

secrets_readable.description: False when the saved secrets can't be opened with this instance's keys (restored without them); replace them.

NotificationChannel.description: Secrets (the webhook URL's path and query, signing secret, header value and SMTP password) are write-only: responses carry only whether each is set.

url.description: https:// (http:// only with allow_private). No user name or password. Write-only: omit on update to keep the saved URL.

anyOf.description: Write-only. Omit to keep; null or empty removes it.
Write-only, printable ASCII. Omit to keep; null or empty removes it.

security.description: starttls upgrades a plain connection and refuses a server that can't; tls encrypts from the first byte (port 465); none only reaches a relay on the server's own loopback address, with allow_private.

anyOf.description: Write-only. Omit to keep; null or empty removes it.

revision.description: Required on update, where a stale value returns 409 STALE_REVISION; absent on create.

id.description: Stable per event (and per test or digest): receivers can drop a repeat. A restart during a send can deliver a message twice.

url.description: A dashboard link when VECTORY_PUBLIC_URL is set.

count.description: Digests only: how many notifications it summarises.

NotificationEvent.description: The machine-readable event in every webhook body, beside Slack's text and blocks. Headers: X-Vectory-Event (type), X-Vectory-Delivery (delivery ID) and, with a signing secret, X-Vectory-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">.

status_code.description: HTTP status, or the SMTP reply code.

outcome.description: retrying: failed, next attempt at next_attempt_at. failed: refused in a way a retry won't fix (address policy, a 4xx other than 408, 425 and 429). gave_up: the fourth attempt failed.

error.description: Bounded; secrets, URL paths and receiver echoes of them are redacted.

DetectionThresholds.description: The editable part of data-plane detection (see Data-plane health). Defaults equal the evaluator's constants.
